title: Hotels Near Bumrungrad International Hospital, Bangkok 2026 — 8 Closest Stays + Booking Links | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: The 8 closest hotels to Bumrungrad International Hospital in Bangkok — each with the real walking or driving distance to Bumrungrad, what it's best for, approximate starting prices and booking links. Made for patients and their families.
ogDesc: The 8 closest stays to Bumrungrad, with real distances and prices.
intro: The Nana–Asok area around Bumrungrad is very easy to get around if your reason for the trip is the hospital. Most hotels sit on Sukhumvit Soi 1, 3, and 5, which wrap around the hospital, so you can walk to the entrance in a few minutes. Nana and Phloen Chit BTS stations are about a 10-minute walk, and taxis and motorbike taxis are everywhere. You'll find convenience stores, food from many countries, and 24-hour pharmacies nearby. It suits patient families, people in for a check-up, and anyone making frequent trips to and from the hospital. The Nana side gets lively with nightlife at night, so if you want quiet, pick somewhere deeper into Soi 1 or Soi 3.

blocks.html: Short answer: Bumrungrad sits on Soi Nana Nua (Sukhumvit Soi 3), and a lot of hotels are within a few hundred metres on foot. For a budget room you can still walk to the hospital from, look at FX Hotel Nana, Zenith Sukhumvit, or FuramaXclusive (from about ฿1,500). For a multi-day or recovery stay with a kitchen, Shama Sukhumvit has serviced apartments. For 4–5 star within walking distance there's Hyatt Place Sukhumvit 1, Ad Lib, and The Landmark. Rates run from roughly ฿1,500 to several thousand a night.

blocks.text: Hotels near Bumrungrad, by distance & budget

items.name: FX Hotel Nana
items.meta: 📍 3-min walk (180 m) to Bumrungrad · ★ 3-star · Best for: Budget · walk to the hospital · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: Sits at the mouth of the soi close to Bumrungrad, a few minutes' walk to the hospital gate. Rooms are simple but clean with a fridge and kettle, and guests rate it well for location and value. A good pick if you just want a tidy bed near the hospital without spending much.

items.name: Zenith Sukhumvit Hotel
items.meta: 📍 4-min walk (300 m) to Bumrungrad · ★ 4-star · Best for: Good value · has a pool · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: On Sukhumvit Soi 3, the same side as Bumrungrad, about 300 metres' walk to the hospital. It has a rooftop pool and several restaurants, with decent-sized rooms at an approachable price. A solid choice for patient families who want a fuller-service hotel without the high rate.

items.name: FuramaXclusive Sukhumvit
items.meta: 📍 4-min walk (230 m) to Bumrungrad · ★ 4-star · Best for: Walk to the hospital · short stays · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: Almost directly opposite Bumrungrad, under 250 metres to walk across, which is handy if you're making several hospital trips a day. Rooms are clean and modern with a small pool, and reviews are generally good. Best for outpatients and families who want to be as close as possible.

items.name: Three Sukhumvit Hotel
items.meta: 📍 2-min walk (130 m) to Bumrungrad · ★ 3-star · Best for: Closest · quiet · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: Right by the Bumrungrad entrance, about 130 metres to the hospital gate. It's a small hotel of around 59 rooms with a quiet feel and friendly service, and reviews praise the cleanliness and location. Ideal for patients and families who value the shortest possible walk.

items.name: Shama Sukhumvit Bangkok
items.meta: 📍 10-min walk (800 m) to Bumrungrad · ★ 4-star · Best for: Long stays · recovery · has a kitchen · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A serviced-apartment property where rooms have a separate kitchen and living area, good for a multi-day or post-treatment recovery stay when you want to cook for yourself. It's about 800 metres from Bumrungrad, walkable or a short taxi ride, with housekeeping and laundry. A fit for families staying a while to care for a patient.

items.name: Hyatt Place Bangkok Sukhumvit 1
items.meta: 📍 2-min walk (130 m) to Bumrungrad · ★ 4-star · Best for: Next to the hospital · families · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: On Sukhumvit Soi 1 right next to Bumrungrad, about 130 metres to walk. It's a Hyatt-brand hotel with newer, good-sized rooms, a pool, and breakfast. Suits families and anyone who wants reliable chain-hotel standards with an easy walk to the hospital.

items.name: The Landmark Bangkok
items.meta: 📍 10-min walk (850 m) to Bumrungrad · ★ 5-star · Best for: 5-star · by Nana BTS · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 5-star hotel on Sukhumvit right by the Nana BTS exit, about 850 metres from Bumrungrad, walkable or a short taxi hop. The building has a classic style with several restaurants and an in-house shopping arcade. Good for anyone who wants a big upscale hotel with easy onward travel by train.

items.name: Ad Lib Bangkok
items.meta: 📍 3-min walk (190 m) to Bumrungrad · ★ 4-star · Best for: Boutique · walk to the hospital · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A leafy boutique hotel about 190 metres from Bumrungrad, a few minutes on foot. It has a pool, a greener and calmer feel than many places in the area, and a shuttle to Nana and Phloen Chit BTS. A fit for anyone who wants a stylish, quiet stay while still being able to walk to the hospital.

faq.q: Are there hotels within walking distance of Bumrungrad?
faq.a: Yes, several. Most hotels around the hospital are on Sukhumvit Soi 1, 3, and 5 and reach the Bumrungrad gate in a few minutes. Three Sukhumvit and Hyatt Place Sukhumvit 1 are about 130 metres away, while FuramaXclusive and FX Hotel Nana are an easy walk at under 250 metres.

faq.q: How do I get to Bumrungrad from Suvarnabhumi Airport?
faq.a: The easiest way is a taxi, about 40–60 minutes depending on traffic. To avoid traffic, take the Airport Rail Link from Suvarnabhumi to Phaya Thai, change to the BTS, and get off at Nana, then a short taxi or motorbike-taxi ride, or a roughly 10-minute walk, to Bumrungrad.

faq.q: What kind of stay is best for a multi-day recovery?
faq.a: If you'll be there several days or recovering after treatment, look at a serviced apartment like Shama Sukhumvit, which has a separate kitchen and living area so you can cook, plus housekeeping and laundry. It's more comfortable than a single hotel room for longer stays with family helping out.
